faq.a: Saltanat is associated with the Arabic form سَلْطَنَت, whose core sense is saltanat; sovereignty, rule.

faq.q: What is the origin of Saltanat?
faq.a: Saltanat is associated with Arabic. Saltanat is Arabic سَلْطَنَة (Salṭana), meaning 'sovereignty, rule'. It is used as a female given name in Central Asia.
Yes — the underlying form سَلْطَنَت is Arabic.
Saltanat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Saltanat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س ل ط is Quranic (authority), but Salṭanat is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Saltanat mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Saltanat is rendered سلطنت and carries the sense سلطنت، حکومت.

faq.q: What does Saltanat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Saltanat is rendered سلطنت and carries the sense سلطنت، فرمانروایی.
A romanized syllable approximation is sal-ta-nat. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Saltanat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Saltanat, saltanat. Script forms are سلطنت, سَلْطَنَت, सल्तनत.

faq.q: Is Saltanat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
